\section*{How to use this dictionary}
Keep it open next to the manual (\href{simplydata_manual.pdf}{\code{simplydata\_\allowbreak{}manual.\allowbreak{}pdf}}).
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=1.6em]
  \item \textbf{Look up a word.} The words are in A to Z order. The words at the top of each page
    are the first and the last word on that page, as in a printed dictionary.
  \item \textbf{Read what it means.} One line says what the word does, in the words of
    \code{sdata.help("word")}.
  \item \textbf{Try the example.} Every example runs as written. Most use a practice table, named
    in brackets after the example: \code{(marks)} means
    \code{table = sdata.table(sdata.example("marks"))} for a table word, or
    \code{chart = sdata.chart(sdata.example("marks"))} for a chart word.
  \item \textbf{Read the page.} \textbf{Manual p.} gives the page of the manual where the word is
    explained in full; the number is a link that opens the manual at that page. \textbf{Lesson}
    gives the lessons that teach it.
\end{enumerate}
Some words belong to more than one thing: \code{save} saves a chart, a table or numbers. Then
the word has one entry with a part for each, marked
\kind{chart}, \kind{table}, \kind{nums} and so on:
\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}ll@{}}
\kind{sdata} \code{sdata.chart(...)} & called on simplydata itself\\
\kind{table} \code{table.keep\_rows(...)} & a step on a table\\
\kind{chart} \code{chart.bars(...)} & a step on a chart\\
\kind{option} \code{show="median"} & an option inside a chart step\\
\kind{nums} \code{nums.average()} & a step on numbers: \code{nums = sdata.numbers([12, 15, 9])}\\
\kind{grid} \code{grid.row(1)} & a step on a grid: \code{grid = sdata.number\_grid([[3, 5], [8, 6]])}\\
\kind{dist} \code{dist.chance(above=60)} & a step on a distribution: \code{dist = sdata.distribution("normal")}\\
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
Know the name from pandas, R, NumPy or matplotlib (\code{groupby}, \code{iloc}, \code{hist},
\code{curve\_fit})? Look it up in \hyperref[other:names]{\textbf{Coming from another tool?}} at the end.

\section*{How the words are built}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.2em]
  \item \textbf{A word says what it does, in full English words}: \code{keep\_rows},
    \code{average\_of}, \code{compare\_averages}. No short forms to remember.
  \item \textbf{Words come in families.} Learn \code{keep\_rows} and you can guess \code{keep\_columns},
    \code{keep\_numbers} and \code{keep\_first\_rows}. The next page lists the families.
  \item \textbf{Steps on a table start with a verb} (\code{keep\_}, \code{remove\_}, \code{add\_},
    \code{make\_}, \code{fill\_}); \textbf{chart types are nouns} (\code{bars}, \code{dots}, \code{histogram}).
  \item \textbf{Anything for one axis ends in \code{\_x} or \code{\_y}}: \code{label\_y},
    \code{range\_x}, \code{log\_scale\_y}. x goes across, y goes up.
  \item \textbf{One option name means one thing everywhere}: \code{for\_each=} (a result for each group),
    \code{between=[low, high]}, \code{colour=}, \code{from\_column=}.
  \item \textbf{Counting starts at 1}, as people count: \code{nums.number\_at(1)} is the first number,
    \code{grid.row(1)} the top row.
  \item \textbf{Every change can be taken back} with \code{undo()}.
\end{itemize}

\section*{The words, A to Z}\label{words}
\begin{dictcolumns}
\letterhead{A}
\headword{absolute\_value}{dict:absolute-value}
\sense{nums}{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}absolute\_\allowbreak{}value()}}
\means{Every number without its minus sign: -3 becomes 3.}
\eg{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}absolute\_\allowbreak{}value()}}
\field{Options}{none}
\field{See also}{\hyperref[dict:square-root]{\code{square\_\allowbreak{}root}}, \hyperref[dict:round-to]{\code{round\_\allowbreak{}to}}, \hyperref[dict:power]{\code{power}}, \hyperref[dict:log]{\code{log}}, \hyperref[dict:divide-by]{\code{divide\_\allowbreak{}by}}}
\where{Manual \manualpage{word:nums.absolute-value}{219}{section*.275}}
\headword{add}{dict:add}
\sense{nums}{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}add()}}
\means{Add a number to every number (or add numbers one by one).}
\eg{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}add(5)}}
\field{Options}{\code{number=}}
\field{See also}{\hyperref[dict:subtract]{\code{subtract}}, \hyperref[dict:times]{\code{times}}, \hyperref[dict:divide-by]{\code{divide\_\allowbreak{}by}}, \hyperref[dict:power]{\code{power}}, \hyperref[dict:square-root]{\code{square\_\allowbreak{}root}}}
\where{Manual \manualpage{word:nums.add}{217}{section*.269}; lesson 13 (\manualpage{lesson:13}{72}{chapter.II.13})}
\headword{add\_adjusted\_p\_value\_column}{dict:add-adjusted-p-value-column}
\sense{table}{\code{table.\allowbreak{}add\_\allowbreak{}adjusted\_\allowbreak{}p\_\allowbreak{}value\_\allowbreak{}column()}}
\means{Adjust p-values for testing many things at once, in a new column.}
\eg{\code{table.\allowbreak{}add\_\allowbreak{}adjusted\_\allowbreak{}p\_\allowbreak{}value\_\allowbreak{}column(\textquotedbl{}q\textquotedbl{},\allowbreak{} method=\textquotedbl{}benjamini-hochberg\textquotedbl{})} \practice{marks}}
\field{Options}{\code{name=}, \code{from\_\allowbreak{}column=}, \code{method=}}
\field{Other tools}{\code{fdr}, \code{multipletests}, \code{p\_\allowbreak{}adjust}}
\field{See also}{\hyperref[dict:compare-shape-to]{\code{compare\_\allowbreak{}shape\_\allowbreak{}to}}, \hyperref[dict:compare-spreads]{\code{compare\_\allowbreak{}spreads}}, \hyperref[dict:compare-counts]{\code{compare\_\allowbreak{}counts}}, \hyperref[dict:compare-counts-to]{\code{compare\_\allowbreak{}counts\_\allowbreak{}to}}, \hyperref[dict:compare-average-to]{\code{compare\_\allowbreak{}average\_\allowbreak{}to}}}
\where{Manual \manualpage{word:table.add-adjusted-p-value-column}{186}{section*.192}; lesson 14 (\manualpage{lesson:14}{76}{chapter.II.14})}
\headword{add\_change\_column}{dict:add-change-column}
\sense{table}{\code{table.\allowbreak{}add\_\allowbreak{}change\_\allowbreak{}column()}}
\means{Add a column with the change from the row before: this value minus the previous one.}
\eg{\code{table.\allowbreak{}add\_\allowbreak{}change\_\allowbreak{}column(\textquotedbl{}growth\textquotedbl{},\allowbreak{} from\_\allowbreak{}column=\textquotedbl{}population\textquotedbl{},\allowbreak{} in\_\allowbreak{}percent=True,\allowbreak{}
                          for\_\allowbreak{}each=\textquotedbl{}country\textquotedbl{},\allowbreak{} sorted\_\allowbreak{}by=\textquotedbl{}year\textquotedbl{})} \practice{growth}}
\field{Options}{\code{name=}, \code{from\_\allowbreak{}column=}, \code{in\_\allowbreak{}percent=}, \code{rows\_\allowbreak{}back=}, \code{for\_\allowbreak{}each=}, \code{sorted\_\allowbreak{}by=}}
\field{Other tools}{\code{diff}, \code{pct\_\allowbreak{}change}}
\field{See also}{\hyperref[dict:add-previous-value-column]{\code{add\_\allowbreak{}previous\_\allowbreak{}value\_\allowbreak{}column}}, \hyperref[dict:add-rolling-column]{\code{add\_\allowbreak{}rolling\_\allowbreak{}column}}}
\where{Manual \manualpage{word:table.add-change-column}{175}{section*.169}; lesson 11 (\manualpage{lesson:11}{57}{chapter.II.11})}
\headword{add\_clusters}{dict:add-clusters}
\sense{table}{\code{table.\allowbreak{}add\_\allowbreak{}clusters()}}
\means{Sort the rows into groups of similar rows (clusters), in a new column.}

\clearpage\section*{Coming from another tool?}\label{other:names}
Names from pandas, Polars, R, NumPy, SciPy, matplotlib and seaborn, and everyday maths words. In simplydata they never run: \code{sdata.\allowbreak{}help(\textquotedbl{}groupby\textquotedbl{})} (or typing \code{table.\allowbreak{}groupby()}) points to the simplydata word. Here each name points to the word and the manual page that explains it. A name that is also a simplydata word is written with its object in front, such as \code{table.\allowbreak{}table}.
